section_summary: This section records merchant vessel arrivals, departures, planned routes, cargo, and bills of health reported by U.S. consular posts in March 1941, usually with a copy forwarded to the Navy. It also includes a report that Osaka Shosen Kaisha ships had been ordered to avoid South African ports, an Auckland report on a changed sailing schedule, and a State Department memorandum on a proposal to limit supplies to Japanese ships in the Philippine Islands.

subfiles.title: Curaçao report on three tanker arrivals
subfiles.about: Reports the arrivals and expected departures of REN, LINCOLN ELLSWORTH, and NORNESS.
subfiles.summary: REN cleared for Cristóbal; destinations of the other two tankers were unknown.

subfiles.title: Tanker movements forwarded to OPNAV
subfiles.about: Relays the Curaçao tanker report to the Navy.
subfiles.summary: Repeats arrivals and departure information for REN, LINCOLN ELLSWORTH, and NORNESS.

subfiles.title: Liaison memorandum and attached tanker paraphrase
subfiles.about: Supplies a confirmation copy of the Curaçao tanker report previously teletyped to OPNAV.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum addresses Captain D. Bode; its enclosure repeats the March 1 Curaçao movements.

subfiles.title: Bombay sailings for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports routes of LONDON MARU and HARUNA MARU departing Bombay on March 2.
subfiles.summary: The two vessels sailed for Japan via Karachi and Singapore, or via Colombo, Singapore, Manila, and Shanghai.

subfiles.title: Singapore Japanese ship movements
subfiles.about: Reports arrivals and departures of four Japanese ships at Singapore.
subfiles.summary: Movements are given for NAGATO MARU, ATLAS MARU, AKATUKI MARU, and AFRICA MARU.

subfiles.title: INDIA MARU bill of health
subfiles.about: Reports a bill of health for INDIA MARU bound for the Philippine Islands.
subfiles.summary: INDIA MARU received a bill of health for the Philippine Islands.

subfiles.title: Simplex Printer transmission slip
subfiles.about: Directs transmission of the preceding report to the Navy.
subfiles.summary: Printer instructions and classification choices for Navy transmission.

subfiles.title: INDIA MARU report forwarded to OPNAV
subfiles.about: Relays the Osaka bill of health report.
subfiles.summary: INDIA MARU is destined for the Philippine Islands.

subfiles.title: BOSTON MARU and DAKAR MARU at Singapore
subfiles.about: Reports two vessel arrivals and departures at Singapore.
subfiles.summary: BOSTON MARU sailed for Batu Pahat; DAKAR MARU sailed for Penang.

subfiles.title: Kobe bills of health for five ships
subfiles.about: Lists bills of health for five Japanese ships bound for North American ports.
subfiles.summary: Destinations are given for KORYU, GYOKO, TATSUTA, KUNIKAWA, and NOSIRO MARU.

subfiles.title: NARUTO MARU cargo at Manzanillo
subfiles.about: Reports NARUTO MARU loading mercury and fluorspar before sailing for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Arriving from Paita, the ship loaded 1,400 mercury flasks and 81 tons of fluorspar, then planned to sail via Los Angeles.

subfiles.title: SIKISAN and LIMA MARU sailings
subfiles.about: Reports sailings toward Legazpi and Calcutta.
subfiles.summary: SIKISAN MARU departed March 5 for Legazpi; LIMA MARU was reported sailing for Calcutta.

subfiles.title: TUSIMA MARU at Barranquilla
subfiles.about: Reports TUSIMA MARU's arrival and onward route.
subfiles.summary: The ship arrived from Cristóbal and planned to call at Curaçao, La Guaira, Philadelphia, and New York.

subfiles.title: RAKUYO MARU at Antofagasta
subfiles.about: Reports RAKUYO MARU sailing from Antofagasta for Hong Kong.
subfiles.summary: The ship arrived from Taltal March 6 and departed March 7 via Los Angeles.

subfiles.title: Four Yokohama sailings
subfiles.about: Reports routes of TATSUTA, MONTREAL, GYOKO, and MELBOURNE MARU.
subfiles.summary: Three ships departed March 6 for Pacific or American destinations; MELBOURNE MARU was reported sailing for Bombay.

subfiles.title: Japanese ships ordered to avoid South African ports
subfiles.from: William C. Burdett, Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: Reports an instruction to Osaka Shosen Kaisha vessels to avoid South African ports.
subfiles.summary: An American Vice Consul at Santos learned of the order from the company's broker.

subfiles.title: Japanese vessel at Santos
subfiles.from: Foster, São Paulo; Department of State
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese ship's arrival from New York and departure for Buenos Aires.
subfiles.summary: The paraphrase names the vessel NANNAM MARU; the original OCR leaves its name uncertain.

subfiles.title: NAKO MARU at Barranquilla
subfiles.about: Reports NAKO MARU's arrival from Cristóbal and planned onward calls.
subfiles.summary: The ship was due to sail March 11 for Curaçao, La Guaira, and New York.

subfiles.title: KIMIKAWA MARU at Manzanillo
subfiles.about: Reports KIMIKAWA MARU unloading cargo and proceeding toward Valparaíso.
subfiles.summary: The ship arrived from Los Angeles, discharged 296 tons, and planned to sail via Punta Arenas and Balboa.

subfiles.title: ANYO MARU at Singapore
subfiles.about: Reports ANYO MARU's arrival and departure.
subfiles.summary: ANYO MARU arrived from Hong Kong March 8 and sailed for India via Penang March 9.

subfiles.title: TOSEI arrival at Vancouver
subfiles.about: Reports the day's Japanese vessel movements at Vancouver.
subfiles.summary: TOSEI arrived from Seattle; there were no departures.

subfiles.title: SYDNEY MARU schedule change
subfiles.about: Reports that SYDNEY MARU will sail directly for Japan instead of visiting Australian ports.
subfiles.summary: The consul also reports scant cargo and a belief that the line is operating at a loss.

subfiles.title: HARUNA MARU at Colombo
subfiles.about: Reports HARUNA MARU's arrival from India and departure toward Manila.
subfiles.summary: The vessel arrived March 9 and was believed to have sailed March 10 via Singapore.

subfiles.title: HEIYO MARU at Manzanillo
subfiles.about: Reports HEIYO MARU's passengers, cargo, and sailing for Acapulco.
subfiles.summary: Thirty-five passengers, including H. Kobayashi, disembarked; Japanese goods were unloaded and merchandise for American ports was loaded.

subfiles.title: HOLLAND and KITANO MARU sailings
subfiles.about: Reports two sailings from Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: HOLLAND MARU reportedly sailed for Melbourne March 8; KITANO MARU sailed March 9 without a stated destination.

subfiles.title: Kobe bills of health for three ships
subfiles.about: Lists bills of health for KENYO, CUBA, and SAKITO MARU.
subfiles.summary: Their stated destinations were San Francisco, Seattle, and the Panama Canal Zone, respectively, with intermediate calls.

subfiles.title: YAMAZUKI MARU sailing for fuel cargo
subfiles.about: Reports YAMAZUKI MARU's departure from Aioi for Los Angeles to load fuel.
subfiles.summary: The ship was bound directly to Los Angeles for oil and gasoline.

subfiles.title: NAKO and TUSIMA MARU at La Guaira
subfiles.from: Bruer, La Guaira; Department of State
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; OPNAV and Coast Guard
subfiles.about: Reports the onward routes of two Japanese ships arriving from Curaçao.
subfiles.summary: NAKO MARU was bound directly for New York; TUSIMA MARU was bound there via Ciudad Trujillo and Habana.

subfiles.title: NAKO MARU at Curaçao
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; OPNAV and Coast Guard
subfiles.about: Reports NAKO MARU's brief Curaçao call.
subfiles.summary: The ship arrived from Iquique March 12 and left the same day for New York via La Guaira.

subfiles.title: DELAGOA and NANKO MARU at Singapore
subfiles.about: Reports arrivals and departures of two Japanese ships at Singapore.
subfiles.summary: DELAGOA MARU sailed for Tuticorin; NANKO MARU sailed for Batu Pahat.

subfiles.title: NANMAN and HAWAII MARU at Montevideo
subfiles.about: Reports planned routes of two Japanese steamers.
subfiles.summary: NANMAN MARU would return from Buenos Aires before sailing to the United States; HAWAII MARU was leaving for South Africa via Brazil.

subfiles.title: CUBA, NAGARA, and KASIMA MARU sailings
subfiles.about: Reports three Japanese ships sailing for North America, the Philippines, and Australia.
subfiles.summary: CUBA MARU sailed for Seattle and Vancouver, NAGARA MARU for Manila and Cebu, and KASIMA MARU for Australia via Philippine ports.

subfiles.title: RAKUYO MARU at Lima
subfiles.about: Reports RAKUYO MARU's movement along the Peruvian coast.
subfiles.summary: The ship arrived from Tambodemora March 13 and sailed for Chancay March 14.

subfiles.title: HIMALAYA and TOBA MARU at Singapore
subfiles.about: Reports routes of HIMALAYA and TOBA MARU.
subfiles.summary: HIMALAYA MARU sailed for Rangoon via Belawan Deli; TOBA MARU sailed for Japan via Shanghai.

subfiles.title: TOYOOKA and AKASISAN sailings
subfiles.about: Reports two March 13 sailings from Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: TOYOOKA sailed for Bombay and AKASISAN for Bangkok.

subfiles.title: TAIHEI, NOSIRO, and HAKODATE MARU sailings
subfiles.about: Reports March 12 departures and an extended American route for NOSIRO.
subfiles.summary: TAIHEI sailed for Portland, NOSIRO for New Orleans via Pacific, Caribbean, and Atlantic ports, and HAKODATE MARU was reported sailing for Calcutta.

subfiles.title: TUSIMA MARU at Ciudad Trujillo
subfiles.from: Lawton, Ciudad Trujillo; Department of State
subfiles.about: Reports a bill of health and onward route for TUSIMA MARU.
subfiles.summary: Arriving from La Guaira, the ship was cleared for New Orleans and eastern U.S. ports via Habana.

subfiles.title: TOEI MARU naval personnel
subfiles.about: Reports TOEI MARU sailing for San Francisco with Japanese Navy personnel aboard.
subfiles.summary: The crew list included 15 naval personnel alongside 45 merchant crew; all had previously voyaged to the United States since February 1.

subfiles.title: AKAGI MARU at Lima
subfiles.about: Reports AKAGI MARU's arrival from Pimentel and departure for Mollendo.
subfiles.summary: The ship arrived March 14 and sailed March 16.

subfiles.title: ARGUN and LONDON MARU at Singapore
subfiles.about: Reports two Japanese vessels sailing onward from Singapore.
subfiles.summary: ARGUN MARU sailed for Japan via Keelung and Shanghai; LONDON MARU arrived from Karachi and left for Japan via Shanghai.

subfiles.title: Japanese sailings and crew conferences at Punta Arenas
subfiles.from: Hornibrook, San José; Department of State
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; OPNAV and Coast Guard
subfiles.about: Reports two Japanese ships bound for Balboa and alleged conferences with German and Italian officers.
subfiles.summary: KIMIKAWA MARU sailed March 15 and TATUNO MARU was sailing March 18. The legation reported closed meetings between Japanese crews and officers of EISENACH and FELLA.

subfiles.title: Proposed limits on supplies to Japanese vessels
subfiles.about: Assesses Singapore's proposal to limit water, coal, and oil supplied to Japanese ships in Philippine ports.
subfiles.summary: British authorities sought limits sufficient for ships to reach their next port, citing concern about supplies reaching enemy raiders and reported Dutch willingness to cooperate. The memorandum reviews voluntary fuel restrictions in the Americas and the Neutrality Act of 1939, finding no apparent legal basis for blanket limits on Japanese merchant ships. It calls for consultation with Philippine authorities, suppliers, the High Commissioner, Army and Navy, and for direct British and Dutch commitments before a decision.
